intention: The /dashboard Vehicle Status panel is regrouped into three named subsections — Travel Progress (latest distance travelled + battery drain), Tire pressure (PSI, one value per wheel with a day-over-day up/down icon), and Interior/Exterior (the existing temperature tiles). vehicle_metrics gains four raw TPMS columns and four TPMS delta _calc columns so the panel reads one precomputed row and computes nothing at request time (Linear MAG-56).
request: /kkpa-pickup-linear-ticket MAG-56 — Vehicle Status Change: add new subsections to the Vehicle Status fields (Tire pressure PSI, Travel Progress) and group the existing interior/exterior fields into their own subsection. Step 1 mirror the tpms_pressure_*_psi columns from telemetry.vehicle_snapshots into analytics.vehicle_metrics with a backfill migration. Step 2 show the latest Distance Traveled and Battery Consumption. Step 3 add four _calc tyre-pressure variance columns compared against the previous date and display them with up/down icons. Do not add cosmetic tests. Use /design for 3 layout suggestions.

decisions.decision: Tyre-pressure variance is stored as four scalar _calc columns (tpms_pressure_fl_psi_calc, _fr_, _rl_, _rr_), not a JSONB blob.
decisions.why: The unit-suffix rule needs a real column to carry _psi. sqlc gives a typed *float64 per column; JSONB gives []byte the gateway must unmarshal by hand. Four wheels is a fixed set.

decisions.decision: Existing rows are backfilled by a cross-schema SQL migration (UPDATE analytics.vehicle_metrics FROM telemetry.vehicle_snapshots). This is an informed deviation from the analytics spec requirement 'No Cross-Module Database Access', and must be recorded as such in the tier design.
decisions.why: User chose it after seeing the recommended watermark-reset alternative and being told it breaks the written rule. It is a one-off data backfill, not a runtime read path.

decisions.decision: The tyre-pressure delta compares against the previous day, same shape as distance_traveled_km_calc. No dead-zone threshold and no target-pressure comparison.
decisions.why: Cheapest option and reuses the existing maths layer. Accepted cost: the delta partly tracks air temperature (~1 PSI per 5.5 C), which is not a defect and must not be 'fixed'.

decisions.decision: Run /design at tier 2 for three Vehicle Status panel layout suggestions. Output must be buildable with Go Templ + htmx and the existing internal/gateway/templates/ui/ kit, not free-form HTML/CSS.
decisions.why: User confirmed the ticket's embedded /design directive, then added the Templ+htmx constraint. Layout does not change what analytics must produce, so it runs at the first gateway tier.

decisions.decision: Tiers alternate analytics -> gateway -> analytics -> gateway, following the ticket's own step order, instead of grouping all backend work first.
decisions.why: Gives a visible screen change after tier 2 and a natural stop point after every tier, which is what the ticket asked for. Cost: two gateway tiers instead of one.

decisions.decision: The label colour from the ticket, rgb(231 189 184 / var(--tw-text-opacity, 1)), is never hardcoded. It maps to the existing semantic theme token.
decisions.why: make ui-guard forbids raw colour values and inline DaisyUI classes. The ticket value was read off an apex screenshot; graphite and halloween must render correctly too.

decisions.decision: The ticket's Step 2 names the wrong endpoint. Travel Progress data comes from the bento path (Handler.dashboardFor, GET /dashboard + /ui/dashboard via LatestMetricsByAccount), not GET /ui/dashboard/history.
decisions.why: The history endpoint renders only the #dashboard-history charts region below the panel. It cannot feed the Vehicle Status panel. Verified in the KB and the handler.

decisions.decision: No cosmetic tests: no template tests coupled to markup, CSS classes, ARIA, or element placement. The pure delta maths in internal/analytics/consumption.go is worth a unit test.
decisions.why: User wrote 'DO not add cosmetic tests' in the ticket. Matches the project's own rule on markup-coupled tests.

decisions.decision: Tier 2 builds layout Option B: an inner 12-col grid inside the panel -- car image plus Odometer and 100% Charges in a 4-col left column, the three named subsections stacked in an 8-col right column. Tire pressure is a 2x2 grid, not one row of four.
decisions.why: User picked it from three /design artboards. It is the most compact option, so the 8-col hero stays close in height to the 4-col column beside it. Cost: 'which wheel' is harder to read than Option C.

decisions.decision: Each tire tile shows the numeric delta as its stat-desc line (e.g. '+0.4 vs prev. day') under the value, in addition to the up/down icon.
decisions.why: The ticket asked only for an icon. User confirmed keeping the number. Tier 3 computes it anyway, so it costs two i18n keys and no new data.

decisions.decision: The ui/ kit gains two things in tier 2: trending_up and trending_down glyphs in ui.Icon, and a trend field on ui.StatTileProps.
decisions.why: The arrows do not exist and StatTile has no slot for an icon. A page hand-writing that markup would bypass the kit, which the module forbids.

decisions.decision: Existing analytics.vehicle_metrics rows get their four tyre-delta _calc values from a backfill migration that self-joins vehicle_metrics on the previous day. Not a watermark reset, not 'wait for the nightly run'.
decisions.why: Tier 1 already copied the raw PSI columns into vehicle_metrics, so the delta is computable inside analytics' own schema. Unlike RD2 this needs no cross-module SQL, and it does not depend on Reconcile recalculating history as a side effect.

decisions.decision: Tier 3 database gate confirmed: four nullable _calc columns, self-join backfill, no new index. A wheel missing its raw reading on either day makes that wheel's delta NULL, not all four.
decisions.why: Columns are projection-only, so an index only costs nightly write time. A 0.0 delta already means 'no pressure change' and must not also mean 'unknown'.

decisions.decision: A real 0.0 tyre-pressure delta shows no icon but keeps its numeric line. A nil delta shows neither. No third neutral glyph.
decisions.why: The roadmap never said what a genuine zero should look like, and only up/down glyphs exist. The number already separates 'no change' from 'unknown'.

Display half of ticket Step 3. Four wheel values with up/down icons from the _calc deltas. A NULL delta renders the value with no icon.
